alignments.note: The Hebrew hearing noun is rendered as a finite subordinate verb.
ASV recasts the idiom 'hearing of an ear' and does not independently represent 'ear.'
ASV supplies 'of me' to state the understood content of the hearing; no source morpheme expresses the pronoun.
The dative preposition is left without an English word before the bare object pronoun.
The construct expression 'sons of foreignness' is rendered by the single substantive 'foreigners'; the supplied article belongs to that substantive phrase.

review_notes: The opening idiom is decomposed where its temporal preposition and hearing lexeme remain independently meaningful; ASV's supplied 'of me' is target-only, while 'ear' is unrepresented.
